name: Alginates
aliases: E400, E401, E402, E403, E404, E405, alginic acid, sodium alginate, potassium alginate, ammonium alginate, calcium alginate, propane-1,2-diol alginate, propylene glycol alginate, hydroxypropyl alginate
what_is: A family of alginic-acid and alginate additives used for gelling, thickening, stabilising and related texture functions. The EU family spans E400–E405, including propylene glycol alginate at E405.
why_botia: Alginates come from brown seaweed and gel when they come into contact with calcium — this is the trick behind spherification, such as liquid popping boba pearls and imitation fish roe. Alginic acid and its salts E400–E404 are not absorbed intact; they reach the large intestine and some of them ferment. In high amounts they can cause digestive discomfort such as gas, bloating or changes in bowel habits, although EFSA found no safety concern at usual food-use levels. Propylene glycol alginate E405 is different: it releases propylene glycol, which is absorbed, and that is why JECFA sets a limit of 0–70 mg/kg body weight per day for it, while no numerical limit was set for E400–E404.
